newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Sandinistas call national strike over property.
newsitem.headline: Sandinistas call national strike over property.

text.p: Nicaragua's Sandinista Front and its affiliated unions have called a national strike for Monday to demand a resolution to Nicaragua's bitter property dispute, a top Sandinista said on Wednesday.

"It's confirmed. There's going to be a national strike on Monday (April 14) involving all Nicaragua's productive sectors. We're going to paralyse the country," Sandinista congressman Juan Manuel Caldera told Reuters.

The strike included plans to block traffic entering the capital Managua and at the country's borders Caldera, former President Daniel Ortega's vice presidential running mate in the 1996 elections, said.

The strikers want the government to negotiate a solution to the property crisis and respect the property of tens of thousands of families who received confiscated land during the Sandinista land reform in the 1980s, he said.

"We are asking for a dialogue to resolve the first basic point, which is property. It is a question of being able to mobilise and give them (landholders) alternatives in order to avoid a confrontation," he said.

The Sandinistas have accused the right-wing government of President Arnoldo Aleman, which took power on Jan. 10, of wanting to roll back the Sandinista land reform and kick thousands of families who received confiscated land off their property and return it to the former owners.

Aleman has denied this accusation, saying he will give poor families who received confiscated land legal titles to the land and will only go after rich Sandinistas who received large confiscated estates and mansions.

While top Sandinistas said the protest would be peaceful, it has stirred fears of violence and Nicaragua's Interior Minister Jose Antonio Alvarado has said authorities would use the police to supress any disorder.
At issue is ownership of more than 200,000 farms, houses and businesses confiscated by the Sandinistas in the 1980s, many of which are being reclaimed by their former owners.
Many Sandinista cooperatives who received confiscated land have vowed to use force to protect their land against any court-ordered eviction.
